newsitem.title: USA: Chrysler 1996 average profit sharing rises.
newsitem.headline: Chrysler 1996 average profit sharing rises.

text.p: Chrysler Corp said Tuesday its average U.S. profit sharing check for 1996 will be $7,900, compared with $3,200 a year ago.
The payment is based on 1996 U.S. pre-tax earnings and will be slightly lower than the record average $8,000 issued two years ago because there are more employees sharing in the money, Chrysler said.

The company said 1996 payments will go to 79,000 U.S. hourly and salaried workers. There were 75,200 workers in the 1994 payment. Chrysler earned $6.28 billion on a pre-tax basis before charges in 1996, and $6.09 billion after the charges.

Chrysler said its average U.S. retail incentive in the fourth quarter of 1996 was $660 a vehicle, up from $495 for the year-ago quarter. But for all of 1996, the average incentive fell to $655 from $770 in all of 1995.

On an after-tax operating basis, per-vehicle profits rose to $1,331 for the fourth quarter from $1,271 in the 1995 fourth quarter. For the year, Chrysler earned $1,183 on an operating basis, compared with $743.
The profit-per-vehicle numbers are before special charges, which totalled $279 million in the fourth quarter of 1996 on an after-tax basis.
Chrysler had fourth quarter net earnings of $807 million after charges, or $1.12 a fully diluted share, down from $1.04 billion or $1.33 a share in the 1995 fourth quarter.
Excluding charges, the 1996 fourth quarter earnings were $1.51, beating the consensus analyst estimate of $1.43, according to First Call.
The company said it completed its $2 billion common stock buyback program for 1996. It has previously announced it expects to repurchase another $2 billion of common stock in 1997.
